title: M0 — the real slice: substrate + exemplar skill + Tier-0 verifier + tier gate (40-bit toy curve end to end)
description:
WHY THIS MILESTONE EXISTS
Cairn is a research harness whose epistemics are immutable and whose strategy is mutable (PLAN §0; CLAUDE.md). M0 builds the one vertical slice everything else plugs into: a content-addressed substrate (SQLite + BLAKE3), one exemplar skill built end to end (content-addressed I/O, captured seed, known-answer self-test, declared cost profile), the Tier-0 verifier (`xP == Q` in a subprocess), and the tier gate with its gate bundle + pin. "Everything else plugs into this shape — get it right once, the verifier included." Build M0 before adding another design layer: a running 40-bit slice reveals more than more architecture.

OPERATOR DECISIONS THAT BIND M0 (confirmed 2026-08-21; recorded in PLAN §16)
(1) PARI-only arithmetic at M0 with the BSGS-vs-SEA *algorithm* cross-check through 50 bits; the gmpy2 Hasse-interval BSGS enters as the *implementation* axis at M1.
(2) One 60-bit rho measured with cypari2 at M0 (bead m0-rho60-measure); a compiled baseline is funded at M1 only if the interpreted rung cannot finish inside the Tier-1 budget.
(8) No separate OS user for the orchestrator before M3; at M0 the gate-bundle pin and the attestation file are protected by file mode/flags only, and the grounding brief records exactly what that does and does not refuse.
(9) A ticket carries its gate-bundle hash; a mismatch re-mints the ticket.

STACK FACTS M0 STANDS ON (probed on this Mac 2026-08-21; research/grounding/pari-sage-toy-curve-backend.md)
PARI/GP 2.17.4 at /opt/homebrew/bin/gp (the shell has `alias gp='git push'` — always use the full path); cypari2 2.2.4 bundles libpari 2.17.2 and produced bit-identical p,a,b,n,tries to gp for the toy-curve search; `ellcard` is milliseconds through 50 bits, ≈75 ms/curve at 60 bits and overflows the default 8 MB PARI stack (use `pari.allocatemem(64_000_000)` / `gp -s 64M`); gp exits 0 on fatal errors (1/0, stack overflow) with the message on stderr, and zero-fills missing arguments; Sage absent; elan/lean absent. M0 re-executes the facts it relies on as tests and records the rest (WAL, busy timeout, append-only flag, write boundary) — bead m0-grounding-probes.

DONE WHEN (PLAN §13 M0):
- the exemplar skill `toy_curve(bits, seed)` runs on a 40-bit toy curve; a deterministic M0 fixture (an integration fixture, not a second research skill) derives `x` and `Q = xP` from that output; the subprocess verifier accepts that pair, rejects a one-coordinate and a one-scalar negative fixture, classifies a forced backend crash as FAIL, and refuses — before the subprocess spawns — a submission that names its own `(P, Q)` rather than the statement node's;
- the generator output, derivation receipt, verifier result and gate-run record are hashed, self-tested, cost-tagged substrate nodes;
- the tier gate refuses a fixture launch declaring a tier two above its ticket and records `TierRefused`; a gate run against a bundle whose hash differs from the pin fails closed;
- a write to the pin and a write to the attestation file, each attempted as the orchestrator's process user, are refused by the operating system, and a `review_verdict` row whose digest matches no attestation record is absent to `justify`;
- `justify` returns STRONG-EMPIRICAL from a synthetic `ladder_table` evidence node with verdict KEEP whose attempt carries a passed reproducibility record, returns the CONJECTURE ceiling for the same table with that record absent or its grade `AuditOnly`, returns a coverage violation when the table's population does not cover the statement's scope, and returns a lattice violation when a synthetic `statistical` node is offered for PROVEN, against a synthetic statement hash;
- a blob unreachable from the roots table is collectable while a rooted one is not;
- the first gate self-tests run before the gates: the verifier's planted `xP ≠ Q` and forced-crash fixtures and the canonicalizer's known-answer vectors for both keys.

SCHEMA-ONLY AT M0 (behavior exercised at M1): budget-ceiling enforcement, escrow reserve/spend/release, yank reach and `disowned` propagation. M0 has a fixture writing and reading each such column. A behavior no M0 test exercises is architecture, not a slice.

ENGINEERING RULES FOR EVERY CHILD BEAD
- Integration test first (real PARI via cypari2, real gp subprocess, real SQLite file), unit tests second.
- Python via `uv` only (`uv run pytest`, `uv add`); never bare pip/python.
- Zero explanatory comments in code; names carry meaning.
- Every child carries a positive observable, a planted negative (a fixture that must FAIL), and a No-Claim line (what green does not prove).
- Closure of a child is a claim until its commands are re-executed at close; paste command + output in the close comment. The epic closes only when `uv run pytest` is green on a fresh clone and `uv run cairn m0-run --bits 40 --seed 1` (bead m0-e2e-slice) produces the four nodes.

NOT IN M0: the ladder, baseline skills, Lean gate, workers, orchestrator, parallel tracks (M1–M4 epics). The research tree is never pre-decomposed into beads (CLAUDE.md).
acceptance_criteria:
- All child beads closed with their own evidence re-executed at close.
- `uv run pytest` green on a fresh clone (integration + unit); output attached to the close comment.
- `uv run cairn m0-run --bits 40 --seed 1` writes four nodes (generator output, derivation receipt, verifier result, gate-run record) with content hashes, self-test references and cost tags; re-running with the same seed reproduces the generator output hash (Replayable).
- Every done-when bullet maps to a named test that was run, with command and output in the close comment.
- No-Claim: M0 green proves the slice's gates refuse the planted fixtures on this Mac; it proves nothing about ECDLP, about any research claim, or about behavior under a second OS user / Linux container.

title: M0: uv project scaffold + real-PARI smoke test (cypari2 in-process + gp subprocess + 60-bit stack fact)
description:
WHY: every later bead runs real PARI through two builds — cypari2 in-process for skills, /opt/homebrew/bin/gp as the verifier subprocess — and real SQLite. Nothing downstream is testable until the toolchain is pinned and a real call succeeds under `uv run`.

WHAT
- `uv init --package` layout: `pyproject.toml` (name `cairn`, Python ≥3.14 — cypari2 2.2.4 ships a 3.14 wheel per the grounding brief), `src/cairn/`, console script `cairn` (argparse is enough).
- Deps: `cypari2` (bundles libpari 2.17.2), `blake3`; dev: `pytest`. `gmpy2` is added at M1 only (operator decision 1).
- Dirs: `tests/integration/` (real PARI/gp/SQLite; the default suite), `tests/unit/`, `tests/e2e/`, `tests/vectors/`, `bundle/` (gate-bundle source), `deploy/` (built bundle + pin + attestation file; gitignored except a README), `var/` (runtime DBs; gitignored). `.gitignore`: `.venv/`, `__pycache__/`, `var/`, `deploy/*.sqlite`, `deploy/*.pin`, `deploy/*.log`.
- `src/cairn/pari.py`: one shared cypari2 handle; `pari.allocatemem(64_000_000)` exactly once at import (the 60-bit `ellcard` overflows the 8 MB default — PROVEN by probe); `GP_BIN = "/opt/homebrew/bin/gp"` with an existence check raising a typed error; `pari_versions()` returning `pari.version()` and the cypari2 version (they feed the environment-manifest digest in bead m0-canon-hash). Never call gp through a shell.
- Smoke tests (integration, `tests/integration/test_smoke.py`):
  (a) cypari2: `ellinit([-3,1],5)` → `ellcard` = 7 (PARI user manual usersch3.tex:29031-29032, upstream_vendored);
  (b) gp subprocess: `subprocess.run([GP_BIN,"-q","-f","-s","64M"], input="print(ellcard(ellinit([-3,1],5)))")` → stdout `7`, rc 0;
  (c) stack fact: `ellcard` on a fixed 60-bit curve succeeds under allocatemem (cypari2) and under `gp -s 64M`; control: the same under `gp -s 8M` fails with a stack-overflow message on stderr and rc 0 (the gp exit-0-on-fatal fact).
- `uv run cairn --version` prints the version.

DESIGN: the PARI handle lives in one module so allocatemem runs once; all gp invocations go through `cairn.pari.run_gp(args, stdin)` returning (rc, stdout, stderr) so later beads share one spawn path.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `uv run pytest tests/integration/test_smoke.py -q` green; three tests visible: cypari2 ellcard=7, gp subprocess prints 7, 60-bit ellcard succeeds under the 64 MB stack.
- Planted negative: 60-bit `ellcard` under `gp -s 8M` must fail with a stack-overflow message on stderr and rc 0, asserted as the expected failure shape; if it unexpectedly succeeds the test fails (the stack fact changed and the verifier's stack ceiling needs re-grounding).
- `grep -r "which gp\|'gp'" src/` finds nothing; the only gp path is `cairn.pari.GP_BIN`.
- No-Claim: green proves the toolchain loads and one known curve order computes; it proves nothing about any skill, gate or timing profile.

title: M0: gate bundle (separate read-only SQLite, content-addressed) + deployment pin (0444) + attestation file (0444+append-only) + attestation digest/offset check + tier gate predicate (TierRefused; bundle≠pin fails closed; uncertified/yanked refused; ticket bundle-hash mismatch re-mints) + OS write-boundary tests + waiver-cannot-advance fixture
description:
WHY (PLAN §4, §5): a gate that silently fails open manufactures the appearance of enforcement. The gate bundle is content-addressed, opened read-only by the orchestrator process, its hash pinned at deployment in an operator-owned file the process user cannot write, and recorded in every gate-run record; a bundle whose hash differs from the pin fails closed whoever rewrote it. The tier gate reads only launch-supplied inputs (cost profile at inputs, budget, hypothesis key/method identity) plus substrate-resolved ones (self-test standing, ticket) and judges against gate-owned objects; a refusal is a `TierRefused` record, not an exception to retry around. Operator decisions 8 (one OS user at M0 → mode/flags only; what that refuses is recorded by bead m0-grounding-probes) and 9 (ticket carries bundle hash; mismatch ⇒ re-mint) bind.

WHAT
- `bundle/*.json` source: `verifier {backend_path:"/opt/homebrew/bin/gp", stack_ceiling:"64M", timeout_s:30, accept:"rc==0 && stdout==OK && stderr==''"}`; `tiers {boundary_table:[{tier:0,max_core_s:1},{tier:1,max_core_s:3600},{tier:2,max_core_h:1000},{tier:3}], ceiling_multiplier:4, tier1_cumulative_edge:null}` (edge set at M1, decision 10); `gate_plan` (ordered steps with expected results — bead m0-gate-plan-selftests); `auditor {f:0.01,bits:20}`; `lean {permitted_axioms:["propext","Classical.choice","Quot.sound"]}` (stored, unused until M1); `role_templates:{}`, `allow_lists:{}` (M1).
- `uv run cairn bundle build --src bundle/ --out deploy/gate-bundle.sqlite`: one row per object (kind, canonical bytes, hash); bundle hash = H('cairn/gate-bundle/v1' ‖ sorted (kind,hash) pairs); deterministic (build twice → same hash). `uv run cairn bundle pin --bundle ... --pin deploy/gate-bundle.pin` writes the hash, chmods pin and bundle 0444. `uv run cairn attest init deploy/attestations.log` creates the file 0444 and sets `uappnd` (macOS; elsewhere logs loudly and skips the flag).
- `GateBundle.open(path, pin_path)`: opens `file:...?mode=ro`; recomputes the hash from rows; compares to the pin; mismatch → `BundlePinMismatch`, and every gate run refuses with a `gate_runs` row `result='refused', reasons=['bundle-hash-ne-pin']`.
- `attestation_record_matches(file, offset, digest) -> bool`: reads the length-prefixed canonical record at `offset`, compares BLAKE3; `visible_review_verdicts(statement_hash)` filters rows through it (used by bead m0-justify). Operator append path: `uv run cairn attest append --kind review_verdict ...` appends the canonical record and mirrors the substrate row with digest+offset (at M0 the same OS user runs both; the boundary is the file mode/flag + the digest rule).
- `TierGate.admit(launch) -> Admitted | TierRefused`; launch = `{cost_profile, inputs, budget_remaining, hypothesis_key, method_identity, statement_hash?, skill_identity_hash, declared_tier}`; resolves `certified(skill_identity)` and not yanked; selects the ticket (Tier 0: none; Tier 1: a hypothesis object, plus the claim statement node where a claim exists, recorded in the substrate; Tier 2/3 kinds are M1 — absent ⇒ refuse); refuses when `declared_tier > ticket_tier + 1` (`tier_refusals` row), when declared tier < the tier the boundary table assigns the production cost, when uncertified or yanked, when declared cost > remaining budget; every decision is a `gate_runs` row with bundle hash + pin hash; a ticket whose recorded bundle hash ≠ current bundle hash → refused `ticket-bundle-mismatch` (re-mint, decision 9).
- Waiver fixture: a waiver record appended through the attestation path does NOT produce a ticket or admit a tier (admission gates are non-waivable, §4).
TESTS (integration, real files under tmp_path): build+pin; open OK; edit one row in a writable copy of the bundle → open refuses, gate_runs row says why; `open(pin,'w')` → PermissionError; `open(attestations,'w')` → PermissionError; `open(attestations,'a')` succeeds and the mirrored review_verdict row is visible only when digest/offset match (forge a row with a wrong digest → absent); launch declaring tier 2 with a Tier-0 ticket → TierRefused row; tier 1 with hypothesis object recorded → Admitted; uncertified skill → refused; production cost above the Tier-1 boundary declared as tier 1 → refused; ticket with stale bundle hash → refused; waiver → no ticket.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `uv run pytest tests/integration/test_gate_bundle.py tests/integration/test_tier_gate.py -q` green; `uv run cairn bundle build` twice → identical bundle hash; deploy/ artifacts created with modes 0444 (pin, bundle) and 0444+uappnd (attestations).
- Planted negative: modified bundle → fail closed with a gate_runs row; tier-two-above → TierRefused recorded; pin write → PermissionError; forged review_verdict digest → absent; waiver → no ticket; stale-bundle ticket → refused. Any of these passing silently fails the bead.
- No-Claim: file mode/flags under ONE OS user — the owning process could chmod them back; M0 records this gap (bead m0-grounding-probes) and decision 8 defers the second OS user to M3; Tier-2/3 ticket kinds and the cumulative edge are M1.

title: M0: declarative gate plan runner with planted-failure self-tests run before the gates (verifier xP≠Q + forced crash; canonicalizer KATs; waiver-cannot-advance); ordered scopes where an earlier failure blocks later steps; fail closed on invalid/missing config
description:
WHY (PLAN §4 gate discipline; §13 M0): every gate ships a planted-failure self-test (a fixture that must FAIL and one that must PASS) run before the gate itself; gates run from a declarative plan with expected results and ordered scopes — an earlier failure blocks later steps and records why; invalid or missing gate config fails closed; a green result whose provenance is weaker than required cannot strengthen a claim. The first gate self-tests at M0 are the verifier's planted `xP ≠ Q` and forced-crash fixtures and the canonicalizer's known-answer vectors for both keys.

WHAT (`src/cairn/gateplan.py`)
- Plan = ordered steps from the gate bundle, e.g. `[{step:'canon_kat', cmd:'kat canon', expect:'pass'}, {step:'verifier_selftest_pass', fixture:'corpus-1 x=3', expect:'OK'}, {step:'verifier_selftest_fail_xP_ne_Q', fixture:'corpus-1 x=4', expect:'FAIL'}, {step:'verifier_selftest_crash', fixture:'60-bit instance, stack 8M', expect:'FAIL backend-crash'}, {step:'waiver_cannot_advance', expect:'no-ticket'}, {step:'tier_gate_selftest_two_above', expect:'TierRefused'}]`; each step writes a `gate_runs` row (gate='gate_plan', plan_step, result, reasons, bundle+pin hash); the first failing step blocks all later steps (`result='blocked', reasons=['blocked-by:<step>']`).
- `GatePlan.run(bundle, substrate) -> PlanResult`; non-zero exit on any failure; a missing plan, an unknown step kind, or a plan lacking any of the required self-test steps (`verifier_selftest_fail_xP_ne_Q`, `verifier_selftest_crash`, `canon_kat`) → fail closed before any step runs (`missing-required-selftest`).
- `uv run cairn gate selftest [--json]`; bead m0-e2e-slice calls it first.
TESTS (integration): full plan green against the built bundle; temp bundle without the `xP≠Q` step → plan refuses to run; monkeypatched always-OK verifier → plan fails at the `xP≠Q` step and later steps are `blocked`; malformed plan row → fail closed; expected-result mismatch recorded with stdout/stderr digests.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `uv run cairn gate selftest --json` exits 0 listing every step `pass` with its gate_runs row id; `uv run pytest tests/integration/test_gateplan.py -q` green.
- Planted negative: an always-OK verifier must make the plan FAIL at the `xP≠Q` step and block the rest; a plan missing a required self-test step must be refused before any step runs. Asserted.
- No-Claim: a green plan proves the fixtures behave as planted on this machine at this bundle hash; it is not evidence about any claim.

title: M0: justify(evidence, statement_hash): kind→max-class map, producer-standing ceiling, coverage check (interval containment / categorical equality / assumption ⊆), lattice violations, review_verdict digest rule, refuted-version rule, append-only attributed tag history
description:
WHY (PLAN §7): the tag is derived, never set. Each evidence kind has a maximum class; `justify` checks the evidence's declared target names the exact statement hash, its declared population is a superset of the statement's scope and its assumptions a subset of the statement's, and returns a typed justification or a lattice/coverage violation — never a boolean. A weaker class may inform, never justify. Every tag transition is an append-only attributed tag_history row with an evidence pointer. PROVEN needs a `lean_artifact` AND an `approve` `review_verdict` on the same statement hash whose digest matches the attestation file (else the row is absent).

WHAT (`src/cairn/justify.py`)
- `justify(evidence, statement, ctx) -> Justification | CoverageViolation | LatticeViolation | Absent | Pending`.
- Kind → max class: `lean_artifact` + visible `approve` verdict on the same statement hash → PROVEN (without it → `Pending(human_review)`, claim stays at its pre-review tag); `ladder_table` verdict KEEP (or KEEP_IN_SAMPLE when the statement scope ⊆ the in-sample sizes) whose own attempt carries a passed reproducibility record → STRONG-EMPIRICAL; same table with the record absent or grade `AuditOnly` → CONJECTURE ceiling; any other table verdict → justifies nothing; `statistical` / `repro_node` → ≤ STRONG-EMPIRICAL on the declared population, EXCEPT for a statement whose typed fields carry a cost model → CONJECTURE ceiling; `model_proof` → ≤ CONJECTURE; `counterexample_hunt_record` SURVIVED → CONJECTURE (a ticket, not a promotion), KILLED → the statement moves to terminal `refuted` with the evidence pointer.
- Producer-standing ceiling: producer is a certified skill revision whose self-test record has no STRONG-EMPIRICAL basis covering the attempt's inputs (every origin `author_supplied`, no randomized-postcondition arm, no cross-check whose independent range contains the inputs) → cap at CONJECTURE.
- Coverage: `population.target_family == scope.target_family`; numeric intervals of the population contain the statement's; `population.assumptions ⊆ statement.assumptions`; otherwise CoverageViolation (typed: which field).
- Disowned evidence (attempt `disowned_at` not null) or `AuditOnly` → Absent. Refuted statement + any positive class → LatticeViolation.
- `derive_tag(statement_hash)` = strongest class justified by any evidence node targeting it; writes a tag_history row (actor 'gate:justify', evidence pointer, typed justification); a downgrade requires an evidence pointer; nothing edited in place.
- `review_verdicts` visible only through `attestation_record_matches` (bead m0-gate-bundle-pin-tier-gate).
- CLI: `uv run cairn justify --statement <hash>` prints the derived tag and the justifying evidence hash.
TESTS (integration, real substrate + attestation file) — the §13 done-when set, named test ids: synthetic statement S (family 'toy_curve', size [30,50], assumptions {A1}); ladder_table KEEP on [30,60] ⊇ scope with passed repro record → STRONG-EMPIRICAL; repro absent → CONJECTURE; grade AuditOnly → CONJECTURE; population [40,50] → CoverageViolation(size_interval); assumptions {A1,A2} → CoverageViolation(assumptions); statistical offered for PROVEN → LatticeViolation; statistical for a cost-model statement → CONJECTURE ceiling; lean_artifact + approve verdict with matching digest → PROVEN; same with a forged digest → verdict absent → not PROVEN (Pending); disowned ladder_table → Absent; statement moved to refuted then a KEEP table offered → LatticeViolation; tag_history holds one row per transition and refuses UPDATE.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `uv run pytest tests/integration/test_justify.py -q` green with every done-when case named in the test ids; `uv run cairn justify --statement <hash>` prints the derived tag and justifying evidence hash.
- Planted negative: statistical→PROVEN must be a LatticeViolation; missing repro must cap at CONJECTURE; forged verdict digest must not yield PROVEN; a coverage gap must be a CoverageViolation. Any of these returning a positive class fails the bead.
- No-Claim: all evidence is synthetic; no ladder, Lean artifact or real verdict exists at M0; the Tier-2/3 branches (KEEP_IN_SAMPLE scope, hunt records) are exercised by construction only.

title: M0: GC roots table + reachability over lineage; only blobs collectable; cache completeness on missing blob; dry-run CLI
description:
WHY (PLAN §3 retention): keep lineage + certificates forever, GC the giant intermediate blobs once their derivation is recorded and the result verified. Roots = recipes, ledger rows, certificates, recorded divergences; liveness = reachability from roots over lineage edges; only blobs are collectable; a cached result is served only if every blob it references is present, otherwise recomputed.

WHAT (`src/cairn/gc.py`): `roots(root_kind, node_hash)`; `reachable()` = BFS from roots over `lineage`; `collect(dry_run)` deletes blob rows not reachable and writes a `gc_runs` record (count, bytes, at); nodes/edges/attempts/receipts are never deleted (append-only triggers from bead m0-substrate-core refuse). `uv run cairn gc [--dry-run]`.
TESTS (integration): recipe R (root) → attempt → manifest → blob B1; orphan blob B2; `collect` removes B2, keeps B1; delete B1's row manually (simulated loss) → `serve(R)` returns None (recompute path; links to the substrate serve test); collect on an empty DB is a no-op; a certificate node is a root and its blob survives; a non-reproducible recipe's two attempts are both rooted (bead m0-substrate-core) and survive.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `uv run pytest tests/integration/test_gc.py -q` green; `uv run cairn gc --dry-run` lists exactly the orphan.
- Planted negative: the rooted blob must survive (collecting it fails the test); gc attempting to delete a node must be refused by the append-only trigger.
- No-Claim: GC over the M0 edge kinds only; the hash-chained log and checkpoint (M2) are not roots yet.

title: M0: end-to-end slice command cairn m0-run: bundle+pin → gate self-tests → certified toy_curve 40-bit → derivation fixture (x, Q=xP) → gate-read verifier → four hashed, self-tested, cost-tagged nodes; negatives recorded; e2e test with logging; fresh-clone run
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `uv run pytest tests/e2e/test_m0_slice.py -q` green; `uv run cairn m0-run --bits 40 --seed 1` exits 0 printing four node hashes + two FAIL negatives; output and the fresh-clone transcript pasted in the close comment.
- Planted negative: pin mismatch ⇒ abort before any skill launch; the one-scalar negative ⇒ FAIL node (an OK there makes the command exit ≠ 0 and the test fail); uncertified skill ⇒ refused.
- No-Claim: a 40-bit toy instance on one Mac; nothing about ECDLP or any research claim; the honest baseline (the 254-bit curve almost certainly stands) is an invariant this slice does not touch.

title: M0: measure one 60-bit Pollard rho with cypari2 (operator decision 2): ops/s, extrapolated wall, a completed 40-bit rho verified by the Tier-0 verifier; record for the M1 compiled-baseline decision
description:
WHY: operator decision 2 — measure one 60-bit rho with cypari2 at M0; fund a compiled rho/BSGS baseline at M1 only if the interpreted rung cannot finish inside the Tier-1 budget (one core, minutes). The ladder's 60-bit rung is tiered by its own declared cost profile (PLAN §5); whether Python-level PARI arithmetic is fast enough decides M1's baseline-skill plan (bead m1-baseline-skills).

WHAT: `scripts/measure_rho60.py` (a measurement, not a skill; not gated): toy_curve(60, seed 1) instance; draw x, Q = xP; Pollard rho with an r-adding walk (r = 20) and distinguished points (θ = 2⁻¹⁰), single-threaded cypari2 `elladd`; expected ≈ √(πn/2) ≈ 1.3×10⁹ group ops at 60 bits, so run with a cap (30 minutes or 10⁸ ops, whichever first) and EXTRAPOLATE from the measured rate, tagging the extrapolation CONJECTURE; also run a 40-bit rho to completion (≈10⁶ ops) so at least one rho finishes and its x passes the Tier-0 verifier (bead m0-tier0-verifier). Record rate, ops counted, extrapolated 60-bit wall, machine, date, tags (STRONG-EMPIRICAL for measured rows) under "rho at 60 bits" in `research/grounding/m0-stack-facts.md`. PARI-only (gmpy2 comparison is M1, decision 1). Run in the background; not on the M0 done-when path.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: the 40-bit rho completes and its x passes the Tier-0 verifier; the 60-bit run records ops/s over ≥10⁷ ops and an extrapolated wall time with its tag; both rows in the grounding brief with commands.
- Planted negative: a planted wrong x from the walk (off-by-one) must FAIL the verifier; the script refuses to report a rate from < 10⁶ ops.
- No-Claim: one seed, one machine, interpreted arithmetic; nothing about any method's asymptotics; the extrapolation is CONJECTURE.

title: M0: execute and record the stack facts M0 stands on (SQLite WAL + busy timeout, macOS append-only flag, pin/attestation write boundary, gp exit/arity facts)
description:
WHY (PLAN §16, §13 M0 first sentence): a stack fact no probe has executed is CONJECTURE until research/grounding/ records the run, and each of these sits under a gate — the single-writer contract relies on WAL + busy timeout (§3); the human path relies on the orchestrator's process user being unable to write the pin or the attestation file (§4); the M2 chain checkpoint relies on the append-only flag binding against truncation (§3). Inherited stack claims are wrong at a meaningful rate when executed.

WHAT: probes as pytest integration tests (they re-run forever) plus the human-readable brief `research/grounding/m0-stack-facts.md` with one row per fact: fact, tag (PROVEN-by-probe / STRONG-EMPIRICAL / CONJECTURE / OPEN), exact command, observed output, date, OS (`sw_vers`, `uname -a`), filesystem (APFS).

PROBES
1. SQLite WAL (`tests/integration/test_grounding_sqlite.py`): file DB under tmp_path; `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` returns `wal`; a reader connection reads while the writer holds an open write transaction. Control: `journal_mode=DELETE` → the reader gets SQLITE_BUSY/blocks.
2. Busy timeout: A holds a write txn; B with `PRAGMA busy_timeout=500` attempts a write → waits ≈0.5 s then `OperationalError: database is locked`; with A committing after 0.2 s, B succeeds. Record measured waits.
3. Append-only flag (`tests/integration/test_grounding_fs.py`, macOS `chflags uappnd` on APFS): on a file owned by the current user with the flag set: `open(path,'a')`+write succeeds; `open(path,'w')` raises PermissionError; `os.truncate` raises; `open(path,'r+')` raises. Control: same ops succeed without the flag. Record honestly: with ONE OS user (operator decision 8) the same user can `chflags nouappnd`, so at M0 the flag refuses truncation by the process but does not bind against a process that clears it — that half is OPEN until M3 introduces the second OS user; the Linux equivalent (`chattr +a`) is OPEN until the M1 container exists.
4. title: M0: canonical typed encoding + BLAKE3 content addressing: recipe key, hypothesis key, identity bundle, environment manifest; known-answer vectors for both keys
description:
WHY (PLAN §3): REFUTED-by-hash and every cache hit are exactly as sound as the canonicalizer — two logically equal recipes that hash differently are a bug that silently under-reports dead ends. The canonicalizer's known-answer vectors are one of the first gate self-tests (§13 M0) and run before any gate.

WHAT (`src/cairn/canon.py`, `src/cairn/keys.py`)
- Canonical encoding: typed, domain-separated; fields in fixed declared order; maps and sets sorted by canonical key bytes; every variable-length field length-prefixed (u64 LE length ‖ bytes); ints as sign byte ‖ big-endian magnitude, length-prefixed (arbitrary precision — curve coordinates are 60–254-bit); strings UTF-8 NFC; blob references as `(hash, size)`; NO unknown fields (a key the schema does not declare raises `CanonError` at write time); no floats in keys (numeric profiles are declared as rationals or strings).
- Hash: BLAKE3-256 over `domain_tag ‖ canonical_bytes`. Fixed domain tags: `cairn/recipe-key/v1`, `cairn/hypothesis-key/v1`, `cairn/node/v1`, `cairn/identity-bundle/v1`, `cairn/env-manifest/v1`, `cairn/selftest-cert/v1`, `cairn/gate-bundle/v1`, `cairn/chain/v1` (reserved for M2).
- Recipe key = H over `(skill_identity_hash, inputs: sorted map name → (hash,size), seed, tool_versions: sorted map, container_digest, salt)`. `skill_identity_hash` = hash of the §2 identity bundle `{interface_version, implementation_revision, tool_digests, container_digest, numeric_profile}` so a changed executable is a different recipe. On the M0 machine (no container) `container_digest` = hash of the environment manifest `{os: sw_vers+uname, python, cypari2, libpari (pari.version()), blake3, gp_binary_sha256}` — never empty (empty raises).
- Hypothesis key = H over the typed hypothesis object `{target_family, claimed_property_or_cost_model (or claim statement hash), method_identity (interface version + canonical params — NEVER implementation revision), declared_parameter_ranges, sampling_distribution?}`; per-run seeds, ladder instances and free-text fields are excluded by schema.
- Schemas: one `Schema` (ordered tuple of (name, type)) per object kind; encode walks the schema, never the dict, so undeclared keys surface as a set difference.
- Known-answer vectors `tests/vectors/canon_kat.json` (≥6): recipe key (two logically-equal spellings with different dict/set order → same expected hash), hypothesis key, identity bundle, env manifest (fixed synthetic values), node hash, and a negative vector (one byte changed in the canonical input → a DIFFERENT expected hash, asserted not-equal). Generated once, committed; origin recorded `author_supplied` (they pin the encoding against drift; they are not an external oracle).
- `uv run cairn kat canon` runs the KAT and exits 0/1 — the entry bead m0-gate-plan-selftests calls.
- Tests (`tests/unit/test_canon.py`): permuting insertion order never changes the hash; undeclared field raises; empty container digest raises; ints round-trip through a decoder used only by tests; every vector matches.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `uv run pytest tests/unit/test_canon.py -q` green; `tests/vectors/canon_kat.json` committed; `uv run cairn kat canon` prints PASS, exit 0.
- Planted negative: the negative KAT vector must NOT match; an undeclared field must raise `CanonError`; an empty `container_digest` must raise. Once at close: flip one byte in a stored vector locally, confirm the KAT test fails, revert; record in the close comment.
- No-Claim: KATs are self-generated; green proves stability of this encoding, not agreement with any external standard; collision resistance is BLAKE3's claim.

title: M0: substrate store (SQLite + BLAKE3): nodes/blobs/lineage, recipes, attempts, execution receipts, cache bits, statuses, salt, disowned, replay grade, certificate slot; single writer + WAL; M1 column fixtures
description:
WHY (PLAN §3): a result not in the substrate does not exist to the claims DB. Provenance is a storage property: every launch appends an attempt; nothing is overwritten; a cached value is served only from a verified attempt; a failure is a record, not a memo. This schema is the shape every later milestone plugs into.

WHAT (`src/cairn/substrate.py`, SQL in `src/cairn/schema.sql`; hashes via bead m0-canon-hash)
Tables
- `blobs(hash PK, size, bytes, created_at)` — the only collectable kind (bead m0-gc-roots).
- `nodes(hash PK, kind, canonical BLOB, replay_grade CHECK IN ('Replayable','Verifiable','AuditOnly'), producer_identity, created_at)`; `lineage(child_hash, parent_hash, edge_kind)` append-only.
- `recipes(recipe_key PK, skill_identity_hash, inputs_manifest_hash, seed, tool_versions_hash, container_digest, salt, do_not_cache INT)`.
- `attempts(attempt_id PK, recipe_key, output_manifest_hash NULL, receipt_hash NULL, status CHECK IN ('OK','FAIL','DISAGREE','BUDGET_EXCEEDED','SKILL_YANKED','INTERRUPTED'), replay_grade, verifier_result_hash NULL, certificate_hash NULL, skip_cache_lookup INT, disowned_at NULL, inadmissible INT DEFAULT 0, started_at, ended_at NULL)`.
- `receipts(receipt_hash PK, gate_bundle_hash, start_mono, end_mono, cpu_user_s, cpu_sys_s, wall_s, peak_rss_bytes, scratch_bytes_written, exit_status, stdout_digest, stderr_digest, tool_digests_hash)` — written by the harness writer only (bead m0-skill-runner-receipt).
- `yank_records(yank_id, skill_identity_hash, reach_predicate, ruling_ref NULL, created_at)`, `salts(class_key PK, salt)` — schema only at M0.
- `escrow(attempt_id PK, declared_production_cost, declared_verification_cost, reserved, spent_at NULL, released_at NULL, ceiling_multiplier)` — M0 writes and reads every column in a fixture; enforcement is M1 (§13).
Behavior
- Cache serve path `serve(recipe_key)`: the most recent attempt with status OK, not disowned, not inadmissible, recipe not `do_not_cache`, every referenced blob present (else None → recompute). `status ≠ OK ⇒ never cached` is part of the serve query, not a convention. `skip_cache_lookup` callers always record a fresh attempt.
- Replayable recipe with two OK, non-disowned attempts whose output manifests differ → `mark_non_reproducible(recipe_key)`: both attempts kept, both rooted, both `inadmissible=1`.
- Immutability: `BEFORE UPDATE`/`BEFORE DELETE` triggers on nodes, recipes, receipts, lineage, and on attempts except the one-time NULL→value set of `disowned_at`/`inadmissible` and the NULL→value set of `ended_at`/`status`-from-pending (status is written once at close; model pending as `ended_at IS NULL` with status pre-filled on launch as 'INTERRUPTED'-eligible) → `RAISE(ABORT,'append-only')`.
- Single writer: `Substrate.open(path, role='writer'|'reader')`; writer sets `journal_mode=WAL`, `busy_timeout=5000`, `synchronous=NORMAL`; reader opens `file:...?mode=ro` URI; one writer object per process (module guard). Workers never receive the writer.
- `weaken_grade(node_hash, to)` refuses a strengthening.
TESTS (integration, file DB under tmp_path; `PRAGMA journal_mode` asserted `wal`): recipe + OK then FAIL attempts → serve returns the OK manifest; disown the OK attempt → None; `do_not_cache` recipe never serves; `skip_cache_lookup` records a new attempt on a hit; two differing OK manifests → both kept, rooted, inadmissible, serve None; UPDATE on `attempts.status` of a closed attempt raises; DELETE on a node raises; `disowned_at` settable once; reader connection write → OperationalError readonly; escrow columns written and read back (`tests/integration/test_schema_admits_m1.py`); a missing blob makes serve return None.
DESIGN: SQL in one file; thin typed Python functions; no ORM; insert recomputes the content hash from the canonical bytes and asserts it equals the caller's hash.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `uv run pytest tests/integration/test_substrate.py tests/integration/test_schema_admits_m1.py -q` green against a real file DB; test log shows `journal_mode=wal`.
- Planted negative: UPDATE to a closed attempt's status must raise (append-only trigger); a FAIL attempt must never be served; a recipe with a missing blob must not be served (delete one blob row, assert None). Each asserted as an expected failure.
- No-Claim: M0 proves the schema admits and refuses what §3 names; budget ceiling, escrow spend/release, yank reach and disowned propagation are column fixtures only — their behavior is M1's.

title: M0: claims-layer schema: hypothesis object, claim statement node, typed evidence node, append-only tag history, review_verdict (digest+offset), gate-run record, tickets, TierRefused
description:
WHY (PLAN §4, §7): the tag is derived, never set; every tag, verdict and gate record names an exact content-addressed statement hash; a human verdict enters through one route and is absent unless its digest matches the attestation file. M0 lays these objects down so `justify`, the tier gate and (from M1) the ladder write to one shape.

WHAT (`src/cairn/claims.py`; additions to `schema.sql`; hashes via bead m0-canon-hash)
- `hypothesis_objects(hash PK, canonical, claim_statement_hash NULL, supersedes NULL, created_at)` immutable.
- `claim_statements(hash PK, claim_id, version, informal, formal_source NULL, scope, quantities, source_claim_hash NULL, supersedes NULL, status CHECK IN ('open','refuted','promoted','withdrawn'), created_at)` — `scope` is the typed record `{target_family (categorical), size_interval, param_ranges (axis-aligned intervals), assumption_set (content-addressed ids)}`; immutable except a single open→terminal status transition (trigger refuses a second).
- `evidence_nodes(hash PK, kind CHECK IN ('lean_artifact','ladder_table','repro_node','counterexample_hunt_record','statistical','model_proof'), target_statement_hash, population, assumptions, producer_identity, producer_tag, verdict NULL, attempt_id NULL, repro_record_hash NULL, created_at)`.
- `tag_history(seq PK AUTOINCREMENT, statement_hash, from_tag NULL, to_tag, evidence_hash NULL, justification, actor, at)` append-only; CHECK: a downgrade (to_tag weaker than from_tag) requires a non-null evidence_hash.
- `review_verdicts(row_id, statement_hash, reviewer, verdict CHECK IN ('approve','reject','needs_revision'), checklist_template_hash, gate_bundle_hash, at, supersedes NULL, record_digest, file_offset)` — the mirror of an attestation-file record; readers treat it as absent unless `record_digest` matches the bytes at `file_offset` (function in bead m0-gate-bundle-pin-tier-gate; used by bead m0-justify).
- `gate_runs(run_id, gate CHECK IN ('canon_kat','verifier','tier_gate','self_test','gate_plan'), bundle_hash, pin_hash, plan_step, instance_hash NULL, statement_hash NULL, result, reasons, at)`.
- `tickets(ticket_hash PK, hypothesis_key, method_identity, statement_hash NULL, tier, kind, node_hash, bundle_hash)`; `tier_refusals(id, hypothesis_key, declared_tier, ticket_tier NULL, reason, at)`.
- Typed dataclasses; constructors compute the hash via canon; `write_*` functions only through the single writer.
TESTS (integration): write one of each, read back byte-equal; UPDATE on any immutable row raises; claim statement v2 with `supersedes=v1` is a new hash and evidence attached to v1 is not returned for v2; tag_history downgrade without evidence raises; `status` moves open→refuted once, a second transition raises; a committed example hash per kind in `tests/vectors/claims_kat.json` stays stable.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `uv run pytest tests/integration/test_claims_schema.py -q` green; every object kind has a KAT-stable hash in tests/vectors/claims_kat.json.
- Planted negative: a downgrade tag_history row with NULL evidence must be refused; a second status transition on a refuted statement must be refused; evidence on v1 must not appear for v2. Each asserted as a raise or empty result.
- No-Claim: schema only; `justify` semantics are bead m0-justify; all evidence at M0 is synthetic.

title: M0: exemplar skill toy_curve(bits, seed) → (p,a,b,n,P) on PARI via cypari2: algorithm-axis cross-check (≤50 bits), postcondition arm, declared cost profile measured over ≥50 seeds, content-addressed I/O
description:
WHY (PLAN §2, §13): the exemplar is the one skill built end to end at M0 — typed interface, fixed version, content-addressed I/O, captured seed, self-test, declared cost profile; every research skill from M1 copies its shape. Operator decision 1: PARI-only at M0 with the BSGS-vs-SEA *algorithm* cross-check valid for bits ≤ 50; no second implementation until M1 (gmpy2).

INTERFACE (`src/cairn/skills/toy_curve.py`): `run(bits: int, seed: int) -> ToyCurveOutput{p, a, b, n, P=(x,y), tries, cross_check: {axis:'algorithm', independent_range:'bits<=50', result:'agree'|'untested'}, status:'OK'|'DISAGREE'}`. Declared cost profile `{tier: 0, production: 'c·ln p tries; c per size from the measured table', verification: 'Replayable, Tier-0 re-run'}`; replay grade Replayable; `do_not_cache=False`. Module entry `python -m cairn.skills.toy_curve` reads canonical JSON inputs on stdin and writes canonical JSON output on stdout (the runner contract, bead m0-skill-runner-receipt); the skill never opens the substrate.

ALGORITHM (matches the grounding brief's bench.gp, which gave bit-identical results in gp and cypari2): `setrand(seed)`; `p = randomprime([2^(bits-1), 2^bits])`; loop: `a,b = random(p)`; skip singular (`4a³+27b² ≡ 0 mod p`); `E = ellinit([a,b], p)`; order: bits ≤ 50 → `n = ellcard(E)` (generic path, milliseconds); bits > 50 → `ellsea(E,1)` early-abort (returns 0 on a small factor), then confirm `n = ellcard(E)` under the 64 MB stack; accept iff `isprime(n)`. Then `P = random(E)` non-identity; assert `ellmul(E,P,n) == [0]`.
Algorithm-axis cross-check (bits ≤ 50 only): `ellsea(E)` (SEA) must equal `ellcard(E)` (generic BSGS-family); on mismatch return `status='DISAGREE'` (never OK, never cached) carrying both transcripts and digests for a substrate node; NO silent retry with a third tool. For bits > 50 `result='untested'` (at 60 bits `ellcard` is itself SEA — agreement by construction, no independence claimed). A cross-check that has never disagreed is reported in the self-test ledger as untested-for-disagreement, never as passing.
Randomized postcondition arm on every output: `isprime(n)`; `ellmul(E,P,n)==[0]`; `n ∈ [p+1-2√p, p+1+2√p]`; `ellisoncurve(E,P)`.
Content-addressed I/O: inputs `{bits, seed}` canonicalized; output manifest = canonical bytes of the output hashed (bead m0-canon-hash).
Cost-profile constant: `uv run cairn measure toy-curve-tries --sizes 30,40,50 --seeds 50` records tries for ≥50 seeds per size (mean, sd, min, max, wall) into `research/grounding/m0-stack-facts.md`; the declared profile cites that table (STRONG-EMPIRICAL on the sample), never the 3-seed table (20–220 tries; CONJECTURE on means). Expected shape: geometric, sd ≈ mean, expected tries ≈ c·ln p.
Stack: `cairn.pari` applies `allocatemem(64_000_000)` once before any 60-bit work.
TESTS (integration, real cypari2): seeds 1,2,3 at 30/40/50 bits reproduce the grounding brief's (p,a,b,n,tries) rows bit-for-bit (pins cypari2-vs-gp agreement); 60-bit seed 1 completes via ellsea(E,1)+ellcard within a minute; postcondition arm asserted on every output; double run same seed → byte-identical manifests; different seed → different p; DISAGREE path via monkeypatched `ellsea` returning n+2 at 40 bits → status DISAGREE, both transcripts present, no OK output; singular pair skipped; forced composite n fails the postcondition arm.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `uv run pytest tests/integration/test_toy_curve.py -q` green: 30/40/50-bit outputs for seeds 1–3 equal the grounding-brief rows; double run byte-equal; 60-bit seed-1 run returns prime n with cross_check.result='untested'; the ≥50-seeds-per-size measurement table is committed in research/grounding/m0-stack-facts.md and the declared profile cites it.
- Planted negative: monkeypatched `ellsea` → n+2 must yield status DISAGREE with both transcripts and no OK; a singular pair must be skipped; a forced composite n must fail the postcondition arm. Each asserted.
- No-Claim: gp/cypari2 agreement is one library twice (one implementation) — it proves the binding, not the arithmetic; the algorithm cross-check is independent only for bits ≤ 50; the measured constant is for this machine and these sizes.

title: M0: toy_curve self-test: vendored known-answer corpus (4 cases, origin per field) + ledger + pass floor, randomized_postcondition arm, golden certificate, byte-equal double run, certificate recorded → revision certified
description:
WHY (PLAN §2): a skill's self-test is (i) a vendored known-answer corpus with a per-case ledger `pass | intentional_non_goal | known_gap` and a committed pass floor only an attributed update may raise; (ii) a golden certificate = hash over the canonical transcript of the corpus and the exact outputs — a changed implementation behind the same interface needs a fresh certificate and a mismatch fails closed; (iii) every nondeterminism source pinned and a byte-equal double run asserted. A corpus supplied only by the author is not a self-test (`author_supplied` alone caps results at CONJECTURE, enforced by `justify`'s producer-standing rule). A revision is launchable only once its self-test passed and its certificate is recorded; the tier gate refuses an uncertified revision exactly as a yanked one.

CORPUS (`src/cairn/skills/toy_curve_corpus.json`, origin per field; sources pinned in research/grounding/pari-sage-toy-curve-backend.md §4)
1. F_5: `y² = x³ − 3x + 1`, `n = 7` — `upstream_vendored` (PARI 2.17.4 usersch3.tex:29031-29032). `P=(0,1)`, `Q=3P=(3,3)`, `x=3` derived locally, origin `randomized_postcondition`: every self-test run asserts `ellorder(E,P)=7` and `ellmul(E,P,3)=Q`; never trusted as vendored.
2. GF(101): `y² = x³ + 90x + 44`, `n = 89` (prime), `x = 2`, `Q = 2P` — `upstream_vendored` (Sage 10.6 ell_point.py:4529-4537 + constructor.py:790-791). `P` is not explicit upstream (`E.gens()[0]`) → chosen locally as the least-x non-identity point; origin `author_supplied` for P with the per-run postcondition `ellorder(E,P)=89`, `2P=Q`.
3. 150-bit: `p = 1427247692705959881058285969449495136382746771`, `E=[1,1]`, `P=(831623307675610677632782670796608848711856078, 42295786042873366706573292533588638217232964)`, `n = 1427247692705959881058262545272474300628281448` (composite, even) — `upstream_vendored` (Sage 10.6 ell_point.py:4680-4686); membership/cardinality/big-int path; no x.
4. Negative control: `E=[1,0]/GF(419)`, `P=(-33,8)`, order 21, card 420 — `upstream_vendored` (Sage 10.6 ell_point.py:822-827); asserts `n·Q ≠ O` for a point outside the order-21 subgroup — the must-FAIL fixture of the postcondition.
Randomized_postcondition arm per run: generate a 30-bit curve from a seed committed AFTER the implementation revision is content-addressed (seed = first 8 bytes of H(implementation_revision ‖ 'selftest-seed')), assert the postcondition arm. Verifier-shaped arm (draw x, Q=xP → driver OK; draw x'≠x → FAIL) depends on bead m0-tier0-verifier and is wired in that bead's PR.
LEDGER + FLOOR: each case → `pass | intentional_non_goal | known_gap`; `pass_floor` (M0: 4/4 + arm) lives in the corpus file; only an attributed change (commit with reason) may raise it.
CERTIFICATE: `cert = H('cairn/selftest-cert/v1' ‖ canonical transcript of (corpus, exact outputs, ledger, env manifest))`; substrate table `skill_certificates(identity_bundle_hash, cert_hash, transcript_hash, at)`; `certified(identity_bundle_hash)` ⇔ a row exists whose recomputed transcript hash matches. DOUBLE RUN: the whole self-test runs twice; canonical transcripts byte-equal (no timestamps inside the transcript; seed, hashers, clock pinned). Runtime target < 5 s, Tier-0.
CLI: `uv run cairn selftest toy-curve [--json]` exits 0 and prints the certificate hash; a corpus schema check requires `origin` on every field.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `uv run pytest tests/integration/test_toy_curve_selftest.py -q` green; `uv run cairn selftest toy-curve --json` prints `{pass:4, floor:4, certificate:<hash>, double_run:'byte-equal'}`; a `skill_certificates` row exists for the identity bundle hash.
- Planted negative: (a) alter one expected output in a temp copy of the corpus → certificate mismatch, exit ≠ 0, `certified()` false; (b) the negative-control point must FAIL `n·Q = O` (if it passes, the test fails); (c) bump `implementation_revision` without re-running → `certified()` false for the new identity hash.
- No-Claim: certified ≠ correct beyond the corpus; cases with `author_supplied` fields are capped at CONJECTURE by `justify`; the 150-bit case has no discrete-log component.

title: M0: Tier-0 verifier subprocess (gp): membership n·Q=O then xP==Q; affirmative acceptance (rc==0 AND stdout==OK AND stderr empty); arity/field validation before spawn; explicit stack ceiling; forced crash → FAIL; gate-read instance, submitter supplies x only
description:
WHY: "No submission without a passing verifier (xP == Q) subprocess" is an invariant (CLAUDE.md). Acceptance is affirmative, never residual: gp exits 0 on fatal errors (1/0, stack overflow — PROVEN by probe) and zero-fills missing arguments, so rc==0 is not evidence of anything. The instance is gate-read: the curve, n, P, Q come from the claim statement node or dispatch record, never from the submitter, who supplies x alone — `xP == Q` on an instance the worker chose is a true statement about the wrong problem (PLAN §4).

WHAT (`src/cairn/verifier.py`, `src/cairn/gp/verify.gp`)
- `verify.gp` (shape from grounding brief §3): `verify(p,a,b,n,Px,Py,Qx,Qy,x)`: `ispseudoprime(p)` → nonsingular → `ellisoncurve(E,P)` and `(E,Q)` → `ellmul(E,Q,n)==[0]` (membership FIRST — PARI's generic `elllog` can loop when no solution exists; the verifier never calls a log) → `ellmul(E,P,x)==Q`; prints exactly one line `OK` or `FAIL <reason-codes>`; `quit(0|1)`.
- Driver `Verifier.run(instance: Instance, x: int) -> VerifierResult`: validates arity (exactly 9 fields), every field a non-negative int, `Px,Py,Qx,Qy < p`, `x < n`, `n` inside the Hasse interval of p — BEFORE spawning; spawns `[GP_BIN,"-q","-f","-s",stack_ceiling]` loading `verify.gp` with a single stdin line; backend path, stack ceiling, timeout and accept predicate come from the gate bundle (bead m0-gate-bundle-pin-tier-gate; injected at unit level); accepts iff `rc==0 AND stdout.strip()=="OK" AND stderr==""`; everything else → FAIL with `reason ∈ {xP-ne-Q, Q-off-curve, P-off-curve, nQ-not-O, backend-crash, bad-arity, bad-field, timeout}`; default timeout 30 s.
- Instance binding: `run` takes an `Instance` produced by the gate run (from the claim statement node / dispatch record) and a bare `x`; a `Submission` carrying its own `(P,Q)` is refused with `reason='submitter-named-instance'` before any subprocess is spawned (a spy asserts zero spawns). The result records `instance_hash`.
- Result node `{instance_hash, x, accepted, reason, stdout_digest, stderr_digest, rc, wall_s}` written by the caller's writer (gate_runs row per bead m0-claims-schema).
TESTS (integration, real /opt/homebrew/bin/gp): corpus case 1 (p=5,n=7,P=(0,1),Q=(3,3),x=3) → OK; a 60-bit instance from toy_curve seed 1 with x drawn and Q=xP → OK (≈17 ms); one-coordinate negative (Qy+1 → off-curve; and a different on-curve point → xP-ne-Q); one-scalar negative (x+1) → FAIL xP-ne-Q; wrong n → FAIL nQ-not-O; forced backend crash: stack ceiling `8M` on the 60-bit instance → stderr stack overflow, rc 0 → classified FAIL backend-crash; a killed child (SIGKILL mid-run) → FAIL; missing field / extra field / negative int / x ≥ n → refused pre-spawn (spy: no spawn); `Submission(P,Q,x)` → refused pre-spawn; randomized arm: 20 draws (x, Q=xP) → OK and 20 draws x'≠x → FAIL.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `uv run pytest tests/integration/test_verifier.py -q` green with real gp; close comment includes the forced-crash case output (stderr content, rc 0, verdict FAIL).
- Planted negative: the `xP ≠ Q` fixture must FAIL; the forced crash must FAIL (either returning OK fails the test — this pair is the gate's planted self-test wired by bead m0-gate-plan-selftests); a submitter-named instance must be refused with zero subprocess spawns.
- No-Claim: OK proves the discrete log of that bound instance; nothing about how x was found, its cost, or any research claim; x and instances are toy-scale and the subprocess is unsandboxed (macOS dev shape).

title: M0: skill runner: subprocess launch with content-addressed inputs, harness-written execution receipt (CPU/wall/RSS/scratch bytes/exit/digests/bundle hash), attempt row + statuses, cache bits, 4× wall ceiling on the trivial fixture
description:
WHY (PLAN §3, §5): the execution receipt is the harness's own record of the run, written by the writer and never by the skill; its readers are the budget ceiling, the ladder's clock and memory measurements and the provenance check. A receipt the skill writes about itself is a number from the gated party. Workers are subprocesses that return artifacts to the single writer and hold no write capability.
